records.source_description: Roman Catholic corporal burse, c.1900, independently inventoried as Palissy PM35002705; actual liturgical object. Source photograph not necessarily used in a 1962 Mass.

records.creator: Cooper Hewitt / Matt Flynn (file EXIF)
records.venue: Cooper Hewitt Smithsonian Design Museum, New York, USA
records.source_description: 19th-century wool-and-linen square burse, 27.3 × 28.6 cm, museum type formally 'Burse'; distinguish from a viaticum carrying pouch.
records.curation_notice: Museum catalogue identifies square object; 1962 ceremonial in-use depiction still requires separate source.

records.creator: Eric Polk
records.venue: Mission San Luis Rey, Oceanside, California, USA
records.source_description: Original photography of 18th-century burse from historic Roman Catholic mission. Museum-style photographic evidence, not modern ceremonial use.
records.curation_notice: Check dark surroundings, reflective glass, cropping and legibility at mobile scale.

records.creator: Bobo11
records.venue: Stiftsbibliothek St Gallen ecclesiastical treasury, Switzerland
records.source_description: Source identifies a burse from the church treasury, photographed in 2023 for a Wikimedia CH-supported project. Use this shot only as one candidate; adjacent St Gallen frame numbers may depict the exact same burse.
records.curation_notice: Review whether composition isolates the burse rather than a wide installation view; no other shots of this specimen are ranked independently.

records.creator: Artinpl
records.source_description: Distinct Polish 18th-century chalice veil, Christ at the Column, inventory SZT 2458 MNW, silk and precious-metal threads; a true Catholic liturgical textile, not an Orthodox aër.
records.curation_notice: Museum-flat view establishes design and identity, not the vesting arrangement over a chalice.

records.venue: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, USA
records.source_description: Distinct 16th-century French silk and metal-thread chalice veil, MET accession 16.32.330. Catholic Western textile; not proof of widespread 1962 use.
records.curation_notice: Well-documented object but museum-flat presentation: assess visual impact, textile condition and cropping.

records.source_description: Italian late-18th to early-19th century bobbin-lace chalice veil MET accession 49.32.11. Unlike usual opaque Roman-rite veils, lace construction requires liturgical/context suitability review.

records.creator: Metropolitan Museum of Art (institutional collection image)
records.venue: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, USA
records.source_description: Genuine Spanish gilded-silver paten c.1450–1500, MET accession 17.190.366, flat dish 14.8 cm diameter; different specimen from the existing Portuguese chalice-and-paten ensemble.
records.curation_notice: Exhibit as historical paten reference, not a representative contemporary primary Roman Missal accessory. Byzantine patens, Protestant cup-covers and reproductions excluded.

source_rights_review: Commons source-page author/rights and dimensions checked; CC0, CC BY-SA or Commons public-domain mark recorded, but complete end-use certification, visual-focus and Roman-rite suitability still pending.
curation_policy: Only genuine distinct Roman Catholic liturgical objects may enter the same-object visual comparison. Photographs of Catholic viaticum carrying purses, Byzantine veils/patens, duplicate angles of a single specimen and reproductions are explicitly excluded. Flat museum textile photograph is NOT equivalent to 1962 Mass in-use photograph.
